Rina (CS): Need a tiny customer-facing runbook: when to prefill/prefetch vs do on-demand, short config snippet, and a tiny troubleshooting command. goal: single page for kickoff packs.
Dev (Solutions): Make it copy/pasteable and add a 3-question feedback message we can send after go-live.
Harper (Eng): Include latency vs cost tradeoffs and batching window suggestions. note on KV key composition.
Rina (CS): Draft bullets: 1) Prefill when prompts are predictable (set TTL 3600s default). 2) Use client-side debounce (100-200ms) + server batch window 30-100ms for interactive UX. 3) Turn streaming on for long generative replies; keep it off for short inference calls.
Liam (PM): Add renewal signals: active-user drop of 35% over 14 days -> outreach; no successful smoke test in 7 days -> remind SE.
Dev (Solutions): Pasteable config:
```yaml
prefetch:
  enabled: true
  ttl_seconds: 3600
client:
  debounce_ms: 120
server_batch:
  max_wait_ms: 50
  max_batch_tokens: 1500
streaming:
  enabled_for_long_responses: true
```
Harper (Eng): Dev notes: - batch window: 30-80ms = better latency, 80-200ms = better cost. - KV key: tenant_id|prompt_hash|ver. - streaming costs more CPU per open connection; best for >250 token flows.
Rina (CS): Feedback template (send at day 7): "Quick check: 1) Relevance (1-5) 2) Latency ok? (yes/no) 3) Anything weird? (optional)" Keep it one-liner.
Dev (Solutions): Troubleshooting one-liner for burst issues:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/{tenant}/metrics?window=5m" | jq '{throughput: .throughput, p95: .latency_p95}'
```
